template.name: New Jack Swing
template.about: Swung 808/909 drum rack at 62%, synth bass, brass stabs, bright gated snare.

project.name: New Jack Swing
project.notes:
NEW JACK SWING  (Teddy Riley, Guy, Bobby Brown, Keith Sweat; c. 1987-1993)

SOUND
Hard, swung drum-machine grooves under R&B singing: punchy kick, bright cracking snare,
claps, busy hats (Riley: "16 triplets and then one 16"), synth bass, brass and orchestra
stabs. Around 100-112 BPM (working range; unconfirmed by a primary source).

REFERENCE GEAR (sourced)
- Riley played parts in by hand and kept quantize off on the MPC; early tracks used a Korg
  DDD-1, a Yamaha DX100 bass and an Oberheim DX with detuned drums (RBMA lecture).
- Rows of Akai MPC60s on stage; other producers tried to copy "which swing Teddy Riley had"
  (RBMA Daily oral history). Riley recorded on Sound Tools (Okayplayer).
- MPC swing: 50% straight, 66% triplet, 54-62% loosens 16ths (Roger Linn, Attack Magazine).
- SP-1200 plus TR-808 as the core kit: unconfirmed.

WORKFLOW
Start in the Drums track's Groove pattern (swing 62%). The drum rack plays one-shots synthesized for these templates (CC0, no recordings), in the voice of the machine each channel is named for, with a starter beat in the pattern; replace them with your own samples for the real machine. Program kick/snare/clap, then
hats; for Riley's hat figure set a 1/16T pattern or play hats in by hand with quantize off.
Bass next, then stabs on the offbeats. Brass and orchestra hits answer the vocal.

MIX NOTES
- Gain staging: drums and bass peaking around -10 dBFS before the buses; leave the master
  6 dB of headroom before the limiter.
- Drum Bus: the built-in Compressor as a console-style bus compressor (4:1, 10 ms / 100 ms),
  2-4 dB of gain reduction; Space D with a short room cut off sharply (linear decay to
  silence) for the era's gated snare. Snare bright: lift 5-8 kHz on the snare.
- Stabs: short decays, high-pass around 150 Hz so they do not fight the bass.
- Vocals: a fast compressor then a slow one (the 1176-then-LA-2A idea), 3-6 dB each.
- Era gear: SSL consoles and Lexicon/Yamaha digital reverbs; built-in compression and Space D
  stand in.
- Loudness: streaming plays back near -14 LUFS integrated (Spotify), so a louder master is turned down; keep true peak below -1 dBTP. Working target -10 to -8 LUFS short-term on choruses.

COVERAGE
Good. Missing: real SP-1200/MPC60, 808/909 or LinnDrum samples (synthesized one-shots stand
in), DX100/DDD-1
emulations, an orchestra-hit sample (a Surge XT stab stands in).

SOURCES
RBMA lecture "Teddy Riley"; RBMA Daily "Teddy Riley and New Jack Swing: An Oral History"
(2017); Okayplayer Teddy Riley interview; Attack Magazine, "Roger Linn on swing, groove & the magic of the MPC's timing" (attackmagazine.com); Spotify for Artists, "Loudness normalization" (support.spotify.com/us/artists/article/loudness-normalization).

FREE PLUG-INS (download them before opening the template; a missing one keeps its slot)
- Surge XT (GPL-3.0): https://surge-synthesizer.github.io/
- OB-Xf (GPL-3.0): https://github.com/surge-synthesizer/OB-Xf
- TDR VOS SlickEQ (freeware (free edition, not GE)): https://www.tokyodawn.net/tdr-vos-slickeq/

SETUP (written from this template)
Tempo 106 BPM, 4/4, key Gmin, cycle bars 1-4.

Tracks
- Drums (Instrument, +0 dB) -> Drum Bus
    instrument: Channel Rack (synthesized one-shots of the template samples: Kick (808) = kick-808.wav, Snare (LM-2) = snare-acoustic.wav, Clap (909) = clap.wav, Closed Hat (909) = hat-909.wav, Open Hat (909) = openhat-909.wav, Rim (909) = rim.wav, Snare 808 = snare-808.wav)
    strip FX: Compressor (Threshold -12, Ratio 4, Attack 30, Release 80, Make-up 2)
    region: Step Sequencer pattern with a starter beat (15 steps on), swing 62% (MPC terms), 7 rows = the rack's channels
- Synth Bass (Instrument, -4 dB) -> Music Bus
    instrument: Surge Synth Team: Surge XT: Surge XT patch "Basses/FM Bass 1"
- Brass Stabs (Instrument, -8 dB) -> Music Bus
    instrument: Surge Synth Team: OB-Xf: OB-Xf patch "Brass/Brass Stabs"
    send: Reverb (bus 4) at -16 dB
- Orchestra Hit (Instrument, -10 dB) -> Music Bus
    instrument: Surge Synth Team: Surge XT: Surge XT patch "Chords/Minor Chord Retro Stab"
    send: Reverb (bus 4) at -14 dB
- Keys (Instrument, -9 dB) -> Music Bus
    instrument: Surge Synth Team: OB-Xf: OB-Xf patch "Keys/JX E. Piano 1"
    send: Reverb (bus 4) at -18 dB
- Lead Vocal (Audio, +0 dB) -> Vocal Bus
    strip FX: Compressor (Threshold -20, Ratio 4, Attack 0.5, Release 60, Make-up 3)
    strip FX: Compressor (Threshold -22, Release 300, Make-up 3)
    send: Reverb (bus 4) at -16 dB
    send: Delay (bus 5) at -24 dB
- Backing Vocals (Audio, -6 dB) -> Vocal Bus
    strip FX: Compressor (Threshold -22, Release 300, Make-up 3)
    send: Reverb (bus 4) at -12 dB

Buses (the n-th Aux strip listens to bus n)
- Drum Bus (bus 1): Compressor (Threshold -16, Ratio 4, Release 100, Make-up 2); Space D (Predelay 0, Dry 0, Wet -10, Decay 0.35, End Level 0, IR "00.5s Small Room")
- Music Bus (bus 2): Channel EQ (High 1.5)
- Vocal Bus (bus 3): Compressor (Release 150, Make-up 2)
- Reverb (bus 4): Space D (Predelay 10, Dry -96, Wet 0, Decay 1.2, Decay Curve 1, Output EQ High 1, IR "Plate")
- Delay (bus 5): Tape Delay (Time 424.5, Tone 5000, Ping-Pong 1, Mix 1)

Stereo Out
- built-in effects: Channel EQ (High 1.5); Compressor (Threshold -12, Ratio 2, Attack 30, Release 200)
- plug-ins (after the built-in effects): Tokyo Dawn Labs: TDR VOS SlickEQ: factory preset "2buss Presence"; Lemon Limiter: gain +3 dB, ceiling -1 dB, other settings default

Bring your own samples: no recordings are included.
